- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >5% from recent high, model underestimates further decline; add 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3-day average of forecast is >83, reduce by 2–4% to align with observed downward drift.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.7, use 70% of forecast + 30% of prior 7-day average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use median of 3–5 prior forecasts instead of full 30d projection to avoid overfitting.
